I have other skill and I'm patient and love learning.

It sounds like you're recognizing some positive qualities about yourself, which is great!  Do you think your thought—"I'm terrible and I'll never find a job"—could be an example of *all-or-nothing thinking*? That means seeing things in black and white, like if you're not perfect at everything, you're a complete failure. Or, could it be *overgeneralization*, where you take one experience (not having projects) and assume it applies to everything about your job prospects? Which of those feels more accurate, or are there other thoughts that come to mind?

It sounds like you're recognizing several thoughts that might be contributing to this feeling.  Do any of these terms sound familiar—like they might describe how your thinking is working: all-or-nothing thinking, where things are either perfect or a complete failure; overgeneralization, where one experience makes you assume everything will be bad?
